key_insight: Staged knowledge distillation can turn difficult pixel-based quantum reinforcement learning into a compact-head learning problem, enabling shallow VQC policies to learn useful visual control from a frozen classical encoder.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical hybrid design pattern for building quantum-compatible control agents when end-to-end training from raw images is unstable or too costly.
method: Train a classical visual teacher on pixels first.
Freeze the teacher encoder as a shared feature interface.
Distil teacher policy behavior into compact downstream heads, including angle-encoded or amplitude-encoded VQCs.
evidence_signal: The pipeline was evaluated on CartPole Pixels and Acrobot Pixels, where angle-encoded VQC heads achieved near-teacher performance and amplitude-encoded heads explored extreme compactness.
watch_item: Amplitude-encoded heads are more fragile and budget-sensitive, with higher simulation cost that may limit practical scalability.
paper_title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation
